newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawyer pleads guilty to SEC obstruction.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawyer pleads guilty to SEC obstruction.

text.p: A Florida attorney pleaded guilty in Manhattan federal court to obstructing a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation, officials said on Wednesday.
In entering his guilty plea, Lloyd Schwed of Jupiter, Florida, admitted he offered to destroy two incriminating tapes the SEC was seeking in an investigation.

Schwed who represented several clients in National Association of Securities Dealers arbitration proceedings, instructed the party under investigation to settle the cases with his clients for $1.45 million of which he was to get one third in return for not turning the tapes over to the SEC and destroying them.
Schwed faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine when he is sentenced.
